title: Named type with custom formatting
description: Declare a named type called Bitcoin built on the whole number type, so an amount of currency cannot be mixed up with a plain count. Give Bitcoin a method called String that describes it as text in the form "10 BTC"; that is the method the standard library's formatting package looks for when it renders a value as text, so describing a Bitcoin has to go through it: Bitcoin(10) described as text -> "10 BTC", Bitcoin(0) -> "0 BTC". Also implement a function called Amount that receives a whole number and returns the matching Bitcoin value: Amount(25) -> a Bitcoin worth 25, which describes itself as "25 BTC".
objective: Practice declaring a named type over an existing one and giving it a custom text representation.

title: Method that mutates its receiver
description: Implement a struct type called Wallet that keeps a balance of whole coins. Give it a method called Deposit, which receives an amount and adds it to the wallet's balance, and a method called Balance, which returns the amount the wallet currently holds. A deposit has to change the wallet it was called on rather than a throwaway copy of it, so deposits build up: on a new wallet, Deposit(10) then Balance() -> 10, then Deposit(5) then Balance() -> 15. A wallet that has never been deposited into holds nothing: Balance() -> 0.
objective: Practice writing a method that modifies the value it was called on instead of a copy of it.

title: Signalling failure with an error
description: A wallet keeps a balance of whole coins. Implement a struct type called Wallet with a method called Deposit, which adds an amount to the balance, a method called Balance, which returns the amount held, and a method called Withdraw, which receives an amount and takes it out of the wallet. Withdraw reports back to its caller whether it worked: when the wallet holds enough it takes the amount out and reports nothing wrong, and taking out the entire balance is allowed. When the wallet holds less than the requested amount it leaves the balance untouched and reports a failure whose message reads exactly "cannot withdraw, insufficient funds". From a wallet holding 20: Withdraw(10) -> no failure, then Balance() -> 10. From a wallet holding 20: Withdraw(20) -> no failure, then Balance() -> 0. From a wallet holding 20: Withdraw(100) -> a failure reading "cannot withdraw, insufficient funds", then Balance() -> 20.
objective: Practice reporting failure from a method by returning a failure value, and reporting nothing when it succeeds.

title: Testing both error paths
description: A wallet is already implemented. It holds a balance of whole coins, and depositing adds to that balance. Withdrawing takes an amount out: when the wallet holds at least that much it removes it and reports nothing wrong, and withdrawing the entire balance is allowed. When the wallet holds less than the requested amount it leaves the balance completely untouched and reports the failure value the package exposes under the name ErrInsufficientFunds, whose message reads "cannot withdraw, insufficient funds". Write tests covering three withdrawals: one the wallet can cover, one that takes the entire balance, and one the wallet cannot cover. Check the resulting balance in every case, and for the rejected withdrawal check that the reported failure is the exposed value itself rather than a value that merely carries the same message.
objective: Practice testing both outcomes of an operation that can fail: asserting nothing went wrong on the successful paths, and asserting the exact failure value and unchanged state on the failing one.
